title: Cleaning Out Mom's House? Don't Throw Away These 10 Things Until You Check Them
description:
Cleaning out a parent's house? Before anything goes in the dumpster, check these 10 things families throw away every week — how to recognize each one, what it really sells for (sold prices), and where to sell it. Plus what isn't worth your time, and how a box headed for the trash in Columbus turned into a few hundred dollars and something priceless.

1. The button tin — Bakelite (hot-water smell test). 2. The mixing bowls — bright, glossy vintage Pyrex (dishwasher-faded = little value). 3. The recipe box & cookbooks — check for first editions; scan the handwritten cards. 4. The war box — keep a soldier's named group together; ask the family first. 5. Christmas boxes — old glass ornaments in original boxes. 6. Hand-stitched quilts. 7. Records — most are $1–2, a few are worth much more. 8. Boxed toys. 9. Sterling silverware (look for "sterling" or "925"). 10. The paper — old stamps, documents, uncashed savings bonds.

Not worth much today: most china sets, common figurines and collector plates, encyclopedias, magazine stacks, "brown furniture."
